prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map represents the scene as a smooth brightness gradient along the sloped road surface, receding from about 0.3–1.0 m at the bright bottom edge to over 4–6 m at the dark upper-left corner, while isolating a person walking 1.5–2.5 m ahead and to the right of the camera wearer. This person ahead faces away from the camera wearer without looking back, has their head and upper shoulders cropped above the top frame edge and their forward leg partly occluding their trailing leg, and remains roughly 1.0–2.0 m beyond the camera wearer's own outstretched forearms and feet, which swing within 0.3–0.7 m at the bottom edge. Across the five frames, the ahead person maintains a steady forward distance while drifting slightly further right by frame 5 (where their right arm is partly cropped at the right edge), and the camera wearer's limbs alternately enter the lower view in frames 1, 3, and 4 and retreat below the frame in frames 2 and 5. The depth map makes the vertical elevation of the ahead person's silhouette and the camera wearer's raised arms much easier to distinguish from the flat ground plane than in RGB alone, but it is unreliable in frame-to-frame scale consistency—frame 3 is globally much darker than the other frames—and it inaccurately renders the person's upper back as brighter (nearer) than their lower legs and feet.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels the walking person 1.5–2.5 m ahead and to the right of the camera wearer (facing away, with their head cropped out at the top) as a pink 'person' mask, and intermittently labels the camera wearer's own lower legs and reaching forearms at the bottom edge (0.3–0.8 m below the camera, within the wearer's arm's reach and 1.0–2.0 m behind the person ahead). Across the five frames, the ahead person's mask captures their walking stride—where the tunic and one leg occlude the other leg—and shifts slightly rightward in frame 5, while the camera wearer's limbs appear at the bottom in frames 1, 3, and 4 as they swing forward and drop out of view in frames 2 and 5. Compared to the RGB strip, the masks provide sharp silhouette boundaries that separate the wearer's dark forearms and the ahead person's dark trousers from the similarly coloured dirt road. However, the map is unreliable in instance grouping and classification: it splits single individuals into multiple separate 'person' instances (assigning separate masks to the wearer's left foot and right arm in frames 1 and 4, and splitting the ahead person's right arm into a separate cyan 'person' in frame 3), misses the wearer's shoe in frame 2, and hallucinates 'broccoli' on the upper-left roadside foliage and a 'kite' on the lower-right dirt in frame 1.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely black across the five frames, failing to render any yellow body skeletons for either the camera wearer or the person walking 1.5–2.5 m ahead on the right (who faces away from the camera wearer with their head cropped at the top and one leg partially occluded behind the other during their stride). It detects only a single magenta hand skeleton at the bottom of frames 3 and 4, corresponding to the camera wearer's own left hand (frame 3, bottom centre) and right hand (frame 4, bottom right) swinging forward into view about 0.4–0.6 m below the camera—within the wearer's immediate reach, but roughly 1.5 m behind the person ahead. Across the sequence, the pose detections appear only when the wearer's hands swing upward into the lower frame in frames 3 and 4, disappearing when the arms retreat below the bottom edge in frames 2 and 5. While these magenta skeletons reveal precise finger and palm articulation against the dark road that is blurred in the RGB frames, the pose map is largely unreliable under this steep downward egocentric viewpoint because heavy body cropping at the top and bottom edges causes it to miss the wearer's outstretched hand in frame 1 as well as the entire body and both hands of the person ahead across all five frames.
